clue.text: Let's not have bird shivering — it's uncivilised

parts.note: read with 'shivering', a wish not to have the bird shivering is a call to heat it, so this phrase supplies heat
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone protests that leaving a bird to shiver is a barbaric thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's not have bird shivering' is a cryptic instruction: to stop a bird shivering you would HEAT HEN, which run together give the answer; 'shivering' belongs to the HEAT idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen, used as an adjective, describes someone thought barbarous or lacking in civilised manners.

clue.text: Beauty spot — at city limits?

parts.note: to eye something is to spot or notice it
the limits of the word city are its outer letters, read out as C and Y

explanation.surface: A tourist guide asks whether a picturesque spot lies out at the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city limits' is read literally as 'C and Y', the letters bounding the word city, spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is a colloquial term for someone or something attractive to look at but not much more.

clue.text: Discussion of great intellectuals becomes more stringent

indicators.note: a discussion is spoken, so the clue asks for a word that is heard like the one meaning great intellectuals

parts.note: titans are giants, figuratively people of towering intellect

explanation.surface: A debate about brilliant thinkers grows ever more rigorous.
explanation.walkthrough: TITANS spoken aloud is close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When a rule or control tightens, it is made stricter and more demanding.

clue.text: Kills time: then prescribes first time must be forgotten

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: something forgotten is dropped, so the letter taken from time leaves the word for prescribes, at its earlier occurrence

parts.note: to dictate is to lay down or prescribe

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the second 'time' in the clue, its abbreviation letter

explanation.surface: A doctor's grim schedule: killing time, then writing prescriptions with an early slot cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kills time' looks like idling, but 'Kills' alone is the definition. 'must be forgotten' drops only one of the two Ts in the word for prescribes, the earlier one.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or destroy completely, as a killer of pests does.

clue.text: In Herculaneum I'm inside sewer, doomed

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words, from the end of the town's name onward

explanation.surface: A tourist in the buried Roman town of Herculaneum finds themselves in its drains, fearing the worst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is one who sews, not a drain: Mimi in Puccini's La Bohème is a seamstress who dies of consumption.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's heroine embroiders for a living and is fated to die in the final act of the opera.

clue.text: Curry was one using fish and rice for starter

parts.note: skate is a flat fish

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter of rice is used

explanation.surface: A cook's curry recipe uses fish, with rice served as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' is not the dish but John Curry, the British figure skater who won Olympic gold in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: John Curry was an Olympic champion figure skater, so he was one who skates competitively.

clue.text: Fragranced candle supplier upset wag worth plenty

indicators.note: when something is upset it is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich, distressed partner of a celebrity sells scented candles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wag' is British slang for a footballer's wife or girlfriend, but here it is anagram fodder; 'upset' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress's lifestyle brand Goop notoriously sold a scented candle with a provocative name.

clue.text: Sort of gas enshrouding Belgian battlefield tree

indicators.note: to enshroud is to wrap round, so the gas letters go around the battlefield name

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas
Ypres in Belgium was the site of major First World War battles

explanation.surface: Gas drifts over a First World War battlefield in Belgium, cloaking a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas attacks were a feature of fighting at Ypres, which gives the surface its grim picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a coniferous evergreen, often planted in cemeteries.

clue.text: Brilliant band showing class in Sinatra number

indicators.note: the word for class is placed in the song title

parts.note: My Way is a song famously recorded by Frank Sinatra
ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A dazzling group plays a classy rendition of a Sinatra song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant band' looks like a group of musicians; it is the bright strip of stars across the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Our galaxy appears as a glowing streak of stars stretched across the sky at night.

clue.text: Mr Bean remade involves good film director

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or contain, so one piece goes inside the other
something remade is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remake of the Mr Bean films features a capable director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remade' scrambles MRBEAN to BERMAN, and 'involves' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingmar Bergman was the Swedish director of films such as The Seventh Seal.

clue.text: Antiseptics pioneer takes in northeast one hears

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so the compass letters go within the surgeon's name

parts.note: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: The surgeon who championed antiseptics admits a patient from the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is someone who pays attention to sounds or speech, an audience member.

clue.text: See 15
Anglican thinker covering viewers' angles

indicators.note: the two words cover, and so contain, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A Church of England theologian considers points of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' means eyes: the definition is the corners of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The canthi are the corners where the upper and lower eyelids meet, so angles of the eye.

clue.text: Barrel-maker had succeeded in works without confrontation

parts.note: a cooper makes barrels and casks
to have a meal is to eat it, so had gives ate
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker's success in a factory came without any arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together with others harmoniously, rather than in opposition.

clue.text: Self-interested Pickles accepting money after game?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the name holds the other letters

parts.note: Eric Pickles is a British Conservative politician, a former cabinet minister

indicators.note: money comes after game, so its letters follow

parts.note: Go is a board game
a cent is a coin, so a unit of money

explanation.surface: A politician, accused of self-interest, accepts cash after playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Pickles is a British Conservative politician and former cabinet minister; 'Pickles' is his surname but supplies his first name here. 'after' sets the money behind the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone egocentric thinks only of themselves and their own concerns.

clue.text: Port stores uranium in ramshackle holding area

indicators.note: to store is to keep inside, so the scrambled letters hold the element symbol
something ramshackle is tumbledown and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A port keeps nuclear fuel in a dilapidated storage yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' rearranges HOLDINGAREA, and 'stores' puts U inside to give the Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dún Laoghaire is a ferry port and harbour town just south of Dublin.

clue.text: Cantor was behind this fixed idea

parts.note: set means fixed or established
a theory is an idea or supposition

explanation.surface: A cantor, a synagogue singer, was responsible for some fixed notion.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantor is not a synagogue singer but Georg Cantor, the mathematician who founded the theory of sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Cantor established the branch of mathematics dealing with collections of objects and infinities.

clue.text: Balboa's greeting to Abraham in Californian park?

parts.note: Rocky Balboa, the boxer in the Rocky films, greets people with 'Yo'
Abraham, the patriarch, was a Semite

explanation.surface: An explorer named Balboa hails the patriarch Abraham in a Californian park.
explanation.walkthrough: Balboa suggests the Spanish explorer, but it is Rocky Balboa, Sylvester Stallone's boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a national park in California's Sierra Nevada, famed for its granite cliffs.

clue.text: Peak in clear — one near borders

indicators.note: to border something is to lie around its edges, so the word for near goes around the others

parts.note: near can mean stingy, as can mean
to rid is to clear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A climber clears a summit, and someone close stands at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' is used in its British sense of tight-fisted, giving MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A meridian is the highest point or culmination, as the sun's position at noon.

clue.text: See 7
It takes a crowd gathered outside to cause trouble

indicators.note: the crowd and its article gather round the outside of the other word

parts.note: a gate is the number of spectators at a sporting event

explanation.surface: It takes a mob assembling outdoors to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is the British term for the attendance at a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up unrest or campaign disruptively, causing trouble.

clue.text: Principles not constant in lyric poem

indicators.note: 'not constant' says the constant's letter is dropped from the word for principles

parts.note: a code is a body of principles or rules
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A lyric poem whose principles keep shifting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyrical poem addressed to a subject, usually in an elevated style.

clue.text: Gives gears thrashing — like some white van drivers?

indicators.note: a thrashing churns things violently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A van driver who crunches through the gears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White van man' is the British stereotype of a pushy, bad-tempered van driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereotypical white van driver is known for hostile, pushy behaviour on the road.

clue.text: Where driver starts, about to steer over missile

indicators.note: over says the whole is turned over, read from the end back to the start
about means around, so the golf word goes around the steering word

parts.note: a golf drive starts from the tee
to cox is to steer a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A motorist starting off is about to steer over a projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golf club, not a motorist. 'about' wraps one piece round the other, giving TECOXE, and 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship guided missile.

clue.text: Mental activity is pre-empted by votes against

indicators.note: to be pre-empted is to be beaten to it, so the other word comes first

parts.note: noes are votes against a motion

explanation.surface: A thought process is forestalled by people voting no.
explanation.definitionFit: Noesis is the philosophers' term for the workings of the intellect, cognition.

clue.text: Bird and horse knackered by rodent

parts.note: tit is an old word for a small or worn-out horse
a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A bird and a horse are exhausted by a pesky rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knackered' (British slang for exhausted) is part of the definition of the horse, a tit being a nag.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is the fuller, older name for the tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Northerner will need second home in country

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage, a country home

explanation.surface: A northerner wants a second home in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, the northernmost part of Britain.

clue.text: Couple crossing river that is in grassland

indicators.note: to cross something is to straddle it, so the couple sits over the river letter

parts.note: a couple is a pair
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Two people wade across a river in open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open area of grassland, especially in North America.

clue.text: Not awfully keen about news boss being sharp

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters are mangled
about means around, so the word for keen goes around the boss

parts.note: hot can mean eager or keen
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted newspaper editor is none too enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges NOT to ONT; 'sharp' is the time sense, as in six o'clock sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp after a time means punctually, exactly at that moment.

clue.text: Shows rock debris navvies cleared out

parts.note: scree is loose rock debris on a slope

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its contents removed, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Labourers clear away loose rubble from a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Navvies are British labourers on road or rail works.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a film or programme is to show it.
